CHAPTER ONE

The survey of the eastern parish was completed in the spring of that year, and the results were
entered in the register by the clerk of the vestry. It was found that the number of households had
increased by eleven since the previous survey, chiefly owing to the new cottages built along the
mill road. The rate assessed upon each household was accordingly reduced by a small amount, though
the total collected remained much the same.

The condition of the roads was reported to be poor. The surveyor recommended that gravel be laid
on the lower lane before the autumn rains, and that the ditch beside the common be cleared of the
brambles which had choked it for several seasons. The vestry agreed to the first recommendation
and deferred the second until a further estimate of the cost could be obtained.

A complaint was received concerning the water supply at the north end of the village, where the
pump had been out of order since the winter. It was resolved that a smith be engaged to examine the
mechanism and that the cost be met from the general fund. The churchwardens were asked to report
on the matter at the next meeting.

The accounts for the year were examined and found to be in order. The balance carried forward was
somewhat larger than in the previous year, which the treasurer attributed to the careful management
of the poor relief and to the sale of timber from the glebe.
